title: Customer-facing audit evidence script and objection handling
body:
Purpose
This doc is a field-ready script and evidence map for sellers and CSEs to use when customers ask for concrete audit evidence around SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, data handling, and audit-log behavior. It is intentionally conservative in legal language, focuses on operational evidence, and maps short answers to artifacts we can provide or demonstrate.

Audience
- Sales engineering and solutions CSEs
- Account executives handling enterprise RFPs
- Customer security reviewers during technical due diligence

How to use this doc
- Memorize the 3 core message pillars below.
- Use the evidence map to quickly pull the right artifact or demo.
- Use the objection handling scripts verbatim for common pushbacks.

Core messaging pillars (easily repeatable)
1) We operate with audited controls and third-party attestations: SOC2 Type II and ISO-aligned controls are in place and continuously tested.
2) Data residency and handling are configurable: hosted customers can choose region and dedicated or private deployment for regulated data flows.
3) Transparent telemetry and auditability: request/response metadata, admin audit trails, and immutable audit logs support customer investigations and regulatory needs.

Concise claim language for initial conversations
- "We maintain SOC2 Type II controls across our hosted environment and provide the SOC2 report under NDA during due diligence."
- "For regulated workloads we offer dedicated and private deployment paths with isolated compute and customer-managed keys."
- "Our audit logs capture admin actions, configuration changes, and model-serving events; logs are retained per contract and can be exported for customer audits."

Evidence map — question -> artifact/demo to surface
- "Can you share proof of SOC2?" -> Provide redacted SOC2 report (under NDA). Link: confluence SOC2 evidence index.
- "How do you show data residency?" -> Demo deployment selector in Console + region-specific endpoint hostnames + copy of data flow diagram.
- "What logs do you capture?" -> Show Audit Log Schema (table view) and recent sample logs; explain retention and export process.
- "How are secrets managed?" -> Show KMS integration page, key rotation cadence, and HSM option for Private customers.
- "How do you handle access reviews?" -> Share access control policy excerpt and screenshots of role-based access controls in the Console.
- "Do you surface model changes and rollouts?" -> Provide rollout audit entries that show model version pinning, canary percentage, and timestamped rollback events.

Sample audit-log language (short snippets to include in email or RFP responses)
- "Audit logs include: timestamp, actor id, action type, target resource, request_id, model_version, route, outcome (success/error), and raw latency. Logs are tamper-evident and exported as newline-delimited JSON via secure S3 endpoints or pushed to customer VPC if configured."
- "Operator-level events (deployment, configuration change, key rotation) are recorded in a separate immutable admin log with cryptographic checksums and retention configurable up to X years per contract."

Handling common objections and escalation triggers
- Objection: "SOC2 report not sufficient; we need control evidence."
  - Script: "We can provide control-level evidence (control narratives, test procedures, and supporting artifacts) under NDA. For deploy-specific items (e.g., private key handling), we can arrange a technical session with our security engineering lead and provide demoable artifacts."
- Objection: "How do you prove logs can’t be altered?"
  - Script: "We use write-once object storage for archived logs, maintain append-only admin logs with checksums, and produce signed digests for forensic timelines. For higher assurance we can provide a write-proxy into the customer's logging system or push logs into a customer-managed S3/VPC to satisfy immutability requirements."
- Escalation: If a customer requests legal wording changes to our data handling commitments or retention beyond standard contracts, route to legal and product for a formal review (tag: escalation-legal).

Competitive differentiation bullets (how to position against alternatives)
- Against pure cloud providers: "We provide inference-first observability (token-timing, model-version traces) rather than generic infra logs — it’s built for auditing model serving behavior."
- Against self-hosted runtimes: "We combine a hardened runtime with managed attestations and evidence packaging so procurement cycles are shorter — customers get predictable compliance without building a new audit program."
- Against other API vendors: "We expose clear, exportable audit artifacts and deterministic routing/rollback hooks so you can prove model lineage during compliance reviews."

Example rapid response templates (use these to reply in chat or email)
- RFP snippet: "Redwood provides SOC2 Type II reports under NDA, audit log exports (JSON), deployment/config change history, and documented control narratives. For HIPAA customers we offer BAAs and can support private deployments with customer-managed keys."
- Slack/Email reply: "Happy to share the redacted SOC2 and an audit-log sample — I’ll attach the SOC2 under NDA and schedule a 30-min run-through with our Security CSE to walk the artifacts."

Operational checklist for demos and evidence pulls
- Verify SOC2 report is the latest issued copy and is redacted appropriately.
- Prepare a 5-min Console walkthrough showing region selector, audit log viewer, and key management settings.
- Pre-generate a 7–14 day sample of audit logs with sensitive fields redacted and ensure timestamps are in ISO-8601.
- Confirm the relevant legal contact for NDAs and BAA requests.

Risks and conservative language to avoid overpromising
- Avoid saying: "We guarantee immutability" — instead say "logs are stored in append-only storage with signed digests; customers can also configure direct log export to their system."
- Avoid specific SLA claims about forensic timelines unless covered in contract.

Playbook for escalations during procurement
1) If legal asks for contract-level data residency guarantees beyond our standard regions, escalate to Product + Legal with the procurement questionnaire and requested clause.
2) If security requests on-site/air-gapped evidence, route to Private Deployment engineering for feasibility and timeline.
3) If auditor requests raw PII records or request/response bodies, deny by default and offer scoped redacted examples and an auditor-led session with Data Security team.

Open items / follow-ups
- Create a one-click "export evidence pack" feature for sales that composes: redacted SOC2 report, audit-log sample, console screenshots, and access control policy excerpt (owner: product-hosted-api).
- Define standard redaction rules for audit logs (PII, user tokens, request payloads).
- Build a short recorded demo (3–4 min) for field use showing audit log export and region selection.

Next steps and owners
- Diego Morales: produce a sample audit-log 14-day export with redaction rules applied (due 2025-02-06).
- Priya Nair: coordinate NDA routing and approved SOC2 redacted copy (due 2025-01-22).
- Ethan Park: draft the 3-min recorded demo and host it on internal sales enablement (due 2025-02-14).

Appendix — quick reference snippets
- Allowed customer deliverables: redacted SOC2 report (NDA), audit-log json sample, console screenshots, control narratives, BAA (HIPAA) template.
- Not allowed/require escalation: raw request/response bodies containing PII, unredacted production logs, legal commitments outside standard templates.
